title: Home page redesign
summary: One home page, built on the site's real code, that answers five critiques at once.
why: A player headline and one featured game first, with the creator pitch further down: most visitors come to play, not upload.
One filter bar with sort, players and genre as different controls: today they look alike, so people can't tell what combines.
Cards coloured by where the game runs: people see what they can play right now before clicking.
The update notice only where it applies: a banner on every page trains people to ignore banners.
A heading, alt text and button labels: screen-reader users can't use the page today.

title: Game page for emulator games
summary: A calmer game page for emulator games, built on today's layout and code.
why: Setup steps inside the player: players see how close they are to playing.
One button that names the next step: there's never a question of what to do.
One line of facts under the title: it replaces the mode pill and its extra hint row.
Save and Share by the creator, everything else under "…": rare actions stop crowding out the important ones.
Known issues folded into one line: support questions stop burying the comments, without taking over the page.
A plain "More like this" list: the chips repeated what the title already says.
